sentences.text: Hi, Jane, how you doing?

Yeah, good, thank you.

Sorry, whereabouts?
Whereabouts are you guys based?
We're New York based.
I know Jane is off site.
I'm in our office right now.
But yeah, we have a.

Can do some quick intros on our end.
I'm Max Shiner.

And I'll pass Jane from here.
Great, thanks.

Great.

Sorry, must be.
Must be you, Max.
Yeah, sorry, I'm in the office, so.
A little bit of.
Can't really do much about that.
No worries, no worries.
I couldn't hear myself talk just for a sec.
Yeah, so we work both the buy and the sell side and we operate agencies co, which is our marketplace platform for sell side clients.
So, yeah, be happy to give you any more detail that you're looking for on today's call.

But also our next steps really is to get information about what your strategy is at Samba currently so that we can guide our client before that meeting and give them as much information as possible to make it a valuable use of time for both sides.
Yeah, definitely makes sense, I would say.

You know, for this call, I think I'll probably approach it from more of a financial lens and then Jane will probably approach it from more of an operational and product fit lens so I can kick things off.
First question, stable revenue growth 22 to 24.
What's causing the pretty significant downturn for 25?
Yeah, so the business model for this company previously has been a marketing agency.
So the majority of the revenue that they've been pulling in is for the design work and the other sort of supplementary stuff that went around the platform that they operate.
More recently, particularly in the last 12 months, they've been focused on converting the business into a SaaS business.
And while they've been doing that, they've been moving away from the agency stuff.
So the business is more profitable but less revenue coming in at the top.
That said, they did also lose a big ish client which they feel is just, is just client churn.
They had the client for quite a while and the relationship had sort of moved towards the end of the cycle and the client churned.
But that did represent some revenue as well, as well as the agency work that they'd stopped doing.
What percentage of the 6.3 or just, you know, high level numbers would be that agency component that you know, know now is no longer part of the business model?
I haven't got the exact number in front of me.
My understanding is it was about a million.
So it was a million in revenue annually.
So it was significant.
But they have replaced a lot of that revenue with new clients and their pipeline is really, really strong.
Really strong.
So is the company now focusing more on building that direct relationship with brands versus agencies?
And do, do you see that's how the revenue split is kind of pivoting towards like more direct brands versus agencies.
So they have different types of clients.
So yeah, they are growing the brand direct work, but they also have a lot of supermarkets and retail businesses that are their clients.

And then on top of that, the agencies, I guess I couldn't tell you definitely whether that is agencies per se, but certainly they're selling more licenses for accessing their platform and that's where the majority of their business now is going, is towards these licenses.
Some of those will be marketing agencies.
The business that they have allows marketing agencies to book media, physical media in store at supermarkets and that type of thing.

So, so just to give you a sort of brief overview, if you were say a vodka brand and you were looking to launch a new sort of flavored vodka, you would be able to look at historic marketing across lots of different stores and pick out the ones where they had the, the best vodka purchases.

And then you'd be able to book in a, a campaign that would appear directly on the edges of shelves and you know, sort of real world artifacts, I don't know what you would call them exactly, but basically, you know, sort of cardboard stands and all of that sort of Stuff that comes with campaigns as well as in store media as well alongside of till stuff placed, you know, near the cashiers point, digital media around there as well.
So a lot of that would be agencies I think Jane, but I don't know the exact definition of those licensed clients.
Great.

So I'm not too sure about their gross margin.
Again, I don't have all of the numbers directly in front of me and I'm not a financial guy, I'm more of the networking guy, the sales guy.
I think that their margins are getting better.
That's all I can really speak to with that.
Obviously their SaaS business is now the core focus of all of the business.
The agency work and the other stuff is all being sunsetted quickly.
So obviously as a software business and with less sort of humans involved in having to deliver the work, the margin.
Sorry, I paused there, Max.
It was gross margin.
What was the second half of that question?
Sorry, cash flow, you know, even if it's cash flow burning, neutral generating, that would be super helpful for us as well.
Yeah.
So a lot of this is, I mean it is dynamic right now.
So the business is going through a huge amount of change.
So we are trying to stay on top of the change in their financials.
But I couldn't give you 100% accurate answer to cash burning or generating.
My understanding is they are now generating more profits as they go forward.
They've invested a huge amount of money in the platform over the last couple of years and it's really starting to bear fruit.
You know that as more users come onto the platform they, they actually feed more information into it as well.
Once we give you a demo, Max, you'll really be able to see, I mean there's photographs of, of, you know, installations all across the world and it's all pretty much real time.
It's a fascinating platform that they've got but, but it's, it's an improving business.
It's an improving business, but it's a, it's a short track record versus their agency stuff.
So yeah, we need to get you into the data room I think and have a look and having a look around the up to date financials.

Yeah, just because there's, there's definitely sometimes a disconnect between growing EBITDA and you know, the actual financial performance of the business given, you know, different definitions of EBITDA and kind of understanding that bridge from their bottom line to cash flow really kind of will help us understand as a SaaS business they should be hopefully generating very high gross margins and then cash flow as well.
So I'd be interested in learning a little bit more about that for sure.
Yeah, I think it's a positive story there for sure.
Things are improving on a daily basis.
Daily basis, you know, they're bringing in more, more and more business.
I mean it really is an untapped market as well.
In the us the majority of the business that they actually have is Europe and uk, Australia, those types of markets.
And there's an untapped market for them in the US because there's a huge gap between the sort of top tier owned, you know, Amazon and Walmart who have all of the, this type of software already.
Obviously that's their bread and butter.
And then there's a huge middle tier that really doesn't have access to this kind of software that they've created.
And there's a huge amount of interest in it as well.
So it's a, it's a big play for them to enter the US market.
So Andy, just so I just to confirm my understanding of the product.
So this company plays in the retail media ecosystem and works with agencies and brands to kind of optimize their media spend.
Right.
And then they like the end result is they deliver successful campaigns, insights, generates insights, et cetera.
Yeah, yeah.
So that is the sort of main sort of play.
But there's a huge amount of data in there as well, Jane, that's being shared in, into the platform.

One of the.
I don't know if you have these in the us.
Well, I'm sure you do.

Yeah, like, like loyalty program.
Yes, exactly that, yeah.

So they have a lot of re live data that goes into their systems as well.
And so they have, you know, different types of licenses for the information and also for the media part of it as well, booking in the media and all of that.
The planning side of things.
Got it.
So curious.

I don't understand 100% around how they get that data out, but obviously they're very careful with the way that that works.
But, but it's all right.
I'll be curious.

And I don't know if this company currently has any tv, OTT or streaming data integrated into the platform, but I think that's where we could potentially see an immediate value add as well.
And social synergy.
Yeah, we have spoke about this at length with, with other interested parties.

So yeah, definitely there is, there is an ability to plug into that real time information that comes from other platforms that will inform buying habits, you know, live buying habits in actual retail stores.
So yeah, that's definitely an interesting crossover there, Jane.
I think once you get a demo of what they're doing, I think your brain's going to be popping with lots of ideas of how this can all plug in and work together.

So that, that's the kind of thing really that I want to take back to them and help inform them to, to get, to give you the best out that meeting when we get it set up.

But, but those sorts of numbers I can make sure.
They have to hand for the next meeting.
So that, that can be an answer.

Definitely some retention metrics as well, you know, quarter to quarter.
Yeah, I think those would be pretty standard for us to want to look through, you know, prior to, you know, a full engagement here and then.

Have you had the IM already?
I don't think you have.
Have you.
A lot of that will, will be in the im.

I mean that's the thing.

Yeah.

summary.overview:
- Capital A specializes in buy and sell side marketing services for companies, aiming to enhance marketplace dynamics for sell side clients.  
- Shopper Group is transitioning from a marketing agency to a SaaS platform, with a planned revenue decline in 2025 offset by increased profitability.  
- The new SaaS platform will enable clients to analyze historic retail marketing data, enhancing media placements based on consumer purchasing patterns.  
- The shift to a SaaS model is projected to yield higher gross margins; the company is heavily investing in this transition with a robust pipeline.  
- There is a significant opportunity for Shopper Group to expand its footprint in the U.S. market, currently focusing on Europe, the UK, and Australia.  
- Integration of real-time shopper data will improve campaign insights and strategic planning within the retail media ecosystem.  
- A potential synergy exists between Shopper Group and Samba TV, leveraging first-party TV and streaming data for better attribution of ad exposure to retail purchases.  
- Shopper Group demonstrates strong SaaS retention metrics with low churn rates, successfully acquiring many smaller license clients.  
- Capital A will provide detailed financials and retention metrics in preparation for the next meeting to evaluate the partnership potential.  
- Samba TV collects data from over 48 million devices, enabling expanded audience measurement and identity graphs globally, offering valuable integration possibilities with Shopper Group’s data.
summary.short_summary: The company is shifting from a marketing agency model to a SaaS-focused business, improving profitability while experiencing lower overall revenue. The agency component, previously generating around $1 million annually, is being phased out to prioritize SaaS growth. Despite a recent client churn affecting revenue, there is a strong sales pipeline in place. The SaaS segment is becoming the core of the business, requiring fewer human resources and enhancing profit margins. The retail media platform enables brands and agencies to optimize marketing campaigns using real-time data. A partnership with Samba TV is being explored to leverage data on TV ad exposure and in-store purchasing, aiming to create a closed-loop attribution model. Further financial metrics are needed for due diligence, and next steps include a demo and financial review to evaluate product fit and strategic alignment.
